mainTopic: How far does the גזירה שוה of תושב ושכיר carry פסח rules over to תרומה? It brings in ערלות. It does not bring in אנינות or the rule about uncircumcised sons and slaves.
overview: This amud defends the גזירה שוה of תושב ושכיר, which teaches that a ערל may not eat תרומה just as he may not eat the פסח. First the גמרא shows that the words are extra on both sides, so the גזירה שוה cannot be refuted, even according to רבי אלעזר. Then it tests how far the comparison reaches. Should an אונן be barred from תרומה? No. The verse 'וכל זר' limits the תרומה ban to זרות, while the גזירה שוה still brings in ערלות. The גמרא explains why ערלות is the one included: it has more stringencies, or, as רבא says, it is written in the פסח section itself. Next it asks whether uncircumcised sons and slaves block a man from תרומה. The word 'בו' in 'ומלתה אותו אז יאכל בו' limits that rule to the פסח. A man's own ערלות still blocks him through the גזירה שוה, since others' ערלות cannot be stricter than his own. Finally the גמרא asks what 'בו' teaches by the בן נכר, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The master does not own him, so the words are free
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that a master does not acquire the body of an עבד עברי. So the words תושב ושכיר by פסח are not needed for their plain meaning and are free (מופנה) to teach a גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we see that his master does not acquire him. Here too, by פסח, his master does not acquire him. So the words are written only to be free to teach something else.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its proof that a master does not own an עבד עברי's body. It concludes that the words תושב ושכיר by פסח are extra, so they are available for a גזירה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might have thought the words were needed to tell us that an owned slave is exempt from פסח. Since the master does not really own him, he obviously must bring a פסח anyway. That makes the words extra, and extra words can be used for a גזירה שוה.

keyTerms.meaning: His master acquires him (owns his body)
To make it free (available) for a גזירה שוה

steps.whyThisMatters: A גזירה שוה built on 'free' words is much harder to knock down. That is why the גמרא works to show the words are extra.

phrases.english: So we see that his master does not acquire him.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי לָא קָנֵי לֵיהּ רַבֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: Here too, his master does not acquire him,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the case of פסח.

phrases.english: Rather, it is written to be free.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a proof begun before this passage.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The words תושב ושכיר by פסח are extra, so they are free (מופנה) for a גזירה שוה.

steps.title: Free from only one side, so it can be refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that only the פסח side is free. רבי אלעזר holds that a גזירה שוה free on just one side can teach, but it can also be refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is still free from only one side. And we heard that רבי אלעזר said: if it is free from one side, we learn from it, but we can also refute it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the strength of the גזירה שוה. Since only one of the two verses has extra words, the comparison might be knocked down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 showed only that the פסח words are free. According to רבי אלעזר, a one-sided free גזירה שוה can be refuted if we find a difference between the two cases. So the rule that a ערל may not eat תרומה is not yet secure.

keyTerms.meaning: Free on only one side of the comparison
We learn from it, but we can also refute it

steps.confusionAlert: 'מופנה' does not mean the verse is useless. It means certain words are not needed for their plain meaning, so they are available for a גזירה שוה.

phrases.english: But still, it is free from only one side,
phrases.notes: Only the פסח verse has been shown to have extra words, not the תרומה verse.

phrases.english: and we heard that Rabbi Elazar said:
If it is free from one side, we learn from it, and we can also refute it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conclusion of step 1 as not strong enough.
steps.kashyaTarget: The גזירה שוה of תושב ושכיר from פסח to תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A one-sided מופנה can be refuted according to רבי אלעזר, so the גזירה שוה is weak.

steps.title: The words are extra on both sides
steps.stepSummary: Since the words are not needed for their own meaning, one extra word can be placed on the learning side (תרומה) and one on the teaching side (פסח). That makes the גזירה שוה free from both sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it is not needed for itself, put one extra word on the side that learns and one on the side that teaches. Then it is a גזירה שוה that is free from both sides.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the גזירה שוה is actually free on both sides. So it cannot be refuted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase תושב ושכיר has two words that are not needed for their own meaning. One counts as extra for the תרומה verse and the other for the פסח verse. A גזירה שוה that is free on both sides cannot be refuted, even according to רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Free on both sides, so it cannot be refuted

steps.whatToRemember: A גזירה שוה that is free on both sides cannot be refuted. So the rule that a ערל may not eat תרומה stands firm.

phrases.english: Since it is not needed for its own meaning —
place one on the side that learns
phrases.notes: The 'one' is one of the two extra words, תושב and שכיר.

phrases.english: and place one on the side that teaches,
and it becomes a גזירה שוה
that is free from both sides.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the words are extra on both sides, which upgrades the strength of the גזירה שוה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the פסח side is free, so the גזירה שוה can be refuted.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both sides are free, so the גזירה שוה cannot be refuted.

steps.title: Then an אונן should be forbidden to eat תרומה
steps.stepSummary: If the comparison between פסח and תרומה holds, it should hold all the way: just as an אונן may not eat פסח, he should not be allowed to eat תרומה either.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so: just as an אונן is forbidden to eat the פסח, so too an אונן should be forbidden to eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with the same גזירה שוה. This line sets up the challenge; the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once פסח and תרומה are linked by a גזירה שוה, other rules might carry over too. The law of פסח forbids an אונן, so the comparison seems to forbid him from eating תרומה as well. The גמרא presents this as a difficulty, since the law is not so.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if you accept this comparison)
A mourner on the day a close relative died, before burial

phrases.aramaic: אִי: מָה פֶּסַח אוֹנֵן אָסוּר בּוֹ —
phrases.english: If so: just as with the פסח, an אונן is forbidden to eat it —
so too with תרומה, an אונן should be forbidden to eat it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי: מָה פֶּסַח אוֹנֵן אָסוּר בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the now-strengthened גזירה שוה to draw a conclusion that seems unacceptable.
steps.kashyaTarget: The scope of the גזירה שוה between פסח and תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison is accepted, it should also carry over the rule against an אונן, which is not the law for תרומה.

steps.title: The verse limits the תרומה ban to non-כהנים, not mourners
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא answers that the verse "וכל זר" shows that only זרות disqualifies a person from תרומה, not אנינות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: The verse says "And every foreigner" may not eat holy food. That means: I told you that being a foreigner (a non-כהן) disqualifies, but not being an אונן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 4: why is an אונן allowed to eat תרומה? רבי יוסי בר חנינא points to a verse that limits the ban.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גזירה שוה from Step 3 would seem to copy every פסח rule onto תרומה. But the verse about תרומה names only the זר as barred, and that limits which פסח rules carry over. So אנינות does not transfer.

keyTerms.meaning: An outsider; here, someone who is not a כהן
The status of being a non-כהן
The state of an אונן, a close mourner before the burial
"The verse says": introduces a proof from a פסוק

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said:
The verse says: "And every foreigner" (may not eat holy food),
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:10. Some versions quote only the word "זר" (in round brackets); others quote "וכל זר".

phrases.english: I told you foreignness disqualifies, but not acute mourning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 4 about the אונן eating תרומה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A verse limits how far the גזירה שוה reaches
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every פסח disqualification, including אנינות, carries over to תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse names only זרות for תרומה, so אנינות does not carry over.

steps.title: Then uncircumcision should not disqualify either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: if the verse excludes everything except זרות, it should also exclude ערלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: foreignness disqualifies, but not lack of circumcision!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If "only זרות" excludes אנינות, it should exclude ערלות too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse's limit seems to remove every disqualification except זרות. That would let an uncircumcised כהן eat תרומה, which goes against the accepted law.

keyTerms.meaning: "Say": the גמרא offers another way to read the matter

phrases.english: Say: but not lack of circumcision!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the scope of the verse limit given in Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי בר חנינא's reading of "וכל זר"
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the verse excludes all disqualifications except זרות, then ערלות should be excluded too.

steps.title: The גזירה שוה brings in uncircumcision
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that ערלות is included through the גזירה שוה of תושב ושכיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written "a sojourner and a hired servant"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the גזירה שוה built in Steps 1–3 is what bars a ערל from תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גזירה שוה has to teach something, and ערלות is what it teaches. The verse "וכל זר" then removes אנינות. So one disqualification transfers and the other does not.

keyTerms.meaning: "But it is written!": points to a פסוק that answers the question
"Sojourner and hired servant": the words that link פסח and תרומה

phrases.english: But it is written: "a sojourner and a hired servant"!
phrases.notes: These words appear by both פסח and תרומה. This is the גזירה שוה from the earlier steps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Nothing bars a ערל from תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גזירה שוה bars the ערל, and the verse "וכל זר" frees the אונן.

steps.title: Why include uncircumcision rather than mourning?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the גזירה שוה was given to ערלות and the verse's limit to אנינות, and not the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move by asking why we chose this split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two sources, one that includes and one that excludes, and two cases. Nothing yet tells us which source goes with which case.

keyTerms.meaning: "And what did you see?": why did you choose this option over the other?

phrases.english: And what did you see?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how Steps 5 and 7 divided the two cases.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason ערלות is included and אנינות excluded, rather than the reverse.

steps.title: Uncircumcision is more severe in many ways
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lists five stringencies of ערלות that make it the better case to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that ערלות should be included, since: he is missing an act; the act is on his body; it carries כרת; it existed before the Torah was given; and the circumcision of his sons and slaves holds back his eating the פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ערלות is the more serious condition, so it is the one the גזירה שוה should include.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each point shows how serious ערלות is. A מצוה action is missing from his own body, it carries כרת, the מצוה was given to אברהם before סיני, and it even affects others, since his family's ערלות stops him from eating the פסח. A more serious condition is the more fitting one to include.

keyTerms.meaning: Spiritual cutting off, a severe heavenly punishment
Before the Torah was given at סיני

phrases.english: It makes sense that lack of circumcision should be included,
since (Acts. Karetim. The word. The slave.)
phrases.notes: The words in round brackets are a memory aid, one keyword for each reason listed next. Some versions leave them out.

phrases.english: he lacks an act, and the act is on his body,
and it is punishable by כרת,
and it existed before the divine word,
phrases.notes: He means the מצוה of מילה was already given to אברהם, before סיני.

phrases.english: and the circumcision of his males and slaves holds him back!
phrases.notes: From the פסח: if his sons or slaves are uncircumcised, he cannot eat it (שמות 12:48).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ערלות is more severe for five reasons, so it is the one to include.

steps.title: Mourning has its own stringencies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא counters with three reasons that אנינות might be the more fitting case to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, אנינות should be included, since it can happen at any time, it applies to men and women, and he has no power to fix himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the other way and argues that אנינות could be the stronger case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אנינות can happen again and again, while מילה happens once. It affects both men and women, while ערלות applies only to men. A ערל can fix his status right now, but an אונן cannot fix his. These points weigh against the list in Step 9.

phrases.english: On the contrary: acute mourning should be included,
since it exists at any time,
and it applies to men and women,
and it is not in his power to fix himself!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counters the reasons given in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ערלות is clearly the better case to include
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אנינות has its own stringencies, so the choice is not obvious.

steps.title: Uncircumcision's reasons are more numerous
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that ערלות has more stringencies, five against three, so it wins.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are more numerous.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the debate by counting: ערלות has more reasons on its side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides have real points, so the deciding factor is which side has more. Five reasons outweigh three, so ערלות is included and אנינות is left out.

phrases.english: These are more numerous.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two sides are evenly matched.
steps.terutzMaskana: ערלות has more stringencies, so it is the one included.

steps.title: רבא: mourning for פסח is itself only learned from מעשר
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that even without counting, ערלות must be the one included. It is written in the פסח section itself, while the rule of אנינות for פסח is only learned from מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even without "these are more numerous," you could not say otherwise. Would we leave out ערלות, which is written in the פסח section itself, and learn אנינות from פסח? The rule of אנינות for פסח is itself learned from מעשר!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different and stronger reason for including ערלות and leaving out אנינות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה from פסח most naturally carries over what is written in the פסח section itself, and ערלות is written there. אנינות is not written by פסח at all. It reaches פסח only by a separate derivation from מעשר, so it is a weaker candidate to pass on to תרומה.
steps.whatToRemember: An אונן may eat תרומה but a ערל may not. The verse "וכל זר" limits the תרומה ban to זרות, and the גזירה שוה still brings in ערלות. ערלות wins either because its stringencies are more numerous, or, as רבא says, because it is written in the פסח section itself.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבא's point is that a derivation reaches what is written in the source text itself before it reaches rules that are only derived there.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Even without "these are more numerous,"
you could not say it.
Would we leave out lack of circumcision, written in the פסח itself,
phrases.notes: שמות 12:48: no uncircumcised man may eat of it.

phrases.english: and learn acute mourning from the פסח?!
For the פסח itself we learn it from tithes.
phrases.notes: He means the אונן's ban on the פסח is not written there. It comes from מעשר (דברים 26:14).

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: בְּלָא הָנָךְ נְפִישָׁן נָמֵי לָא מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative answer to Step 8 that does not depend on the counting in Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explicit text versus a derived rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The choice depends only on counting stringencies.
steps.terutzMaskana: ערלות is written in the פסח section itself, while אנינות for פסח is only learned from מעשר, so ערלות is the rule that carries over.

steps.title: Should uncircumcised sons and slaves block תרומה too?
steps.stepSummary: If פסח and תרומה are linked, then the rule from פסח about uncircumcised sons and slaves should also apply to תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the two are linked, then just as with פסח, a man whose sons and slaves are not circumcised may not eat, so too with תרומה, a man whose sons and slaves are not circumcised should not be allowed to eat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the link between פסח and תרומה further. If they are compared, then every rule of פסח should carry over to תרומה, including the rule about uncircumcised sons and slaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With פסח, a man may not eat until all the males of his house, his sons and his slaves, are circumcised. If the גזירה שוה really ties פסח to תרומה, a כהן with uncircumcised sons or slaves should also be blocked from תרומה. But that is not the הלכה, so the גמרא needs to explain why not.

keyTerms.meaning: the circumcision of his male children and his slaves
holds back, blocks (he can't eat until it is done)
the holy portion of produce given to a כהן
if so (if the comparison is valid)

phrases.english: If so: just as with the פסח,
the circumcision of his males and slaves holds him back,
so too with תרומה,
the circumcision of his males and slaves should hold him back!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי: מָה פֶּסַח מִילַת זְכָרָיו וַעֲבָדָיו מְעַכֶּבֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling which case the גזירה שוה covers, the גמרא tests how far the comparison between פסח and תרומה reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: The full comparison between פסח and תרומה through the גזירה שוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the two are linked, every rule of פסח should carry over, including the rule about uncircumcised sons and slaves. That is not the הלכה.

steps.title: The word 'בו' limits the sons-and-slaves rule to פסח
steps.stepSummary: The verse says 'then he shall eat from it'. 'From it' means only the פסח is blocked by uncircumcised sons and slaves, not תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'When you have circumcised him, then he shall eat from it.' The circumcision of his males and slaves blocks him from eating the פסח, but the circumcision of his males and slaves does not block him from eating תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק itself limits this rule. The word 'בו' (from it) shows that the rule about sons and slaves applies only to the פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word 'בו' is read as a limit: only 'from it', the פסח, is he blocked. So even though פסח and תרומה are linked, this one rule stays with פסח and does not carry over to תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: the verse says (a proof from the wording of a פסוק)
from it (read as a limit: only this, the פסח)

phrases.english: The verse says:
"When you have circumcised him, then he shall eat from it."
phrases.notes: שמות 12:44

phrases.english: The circumcision of his males and slaves blocks him, "from it":
from eating the פסח,
but the circumcision of his males and slaves does not
block him from תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: וּמַלְתָּה אוֹתוֹ אָז יֹאכַל בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13 from the wording of the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A limiting word in the verse ('בו') blocks the rule from carrying over.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every rule of פסח carries over to תרומה through the גזירה שוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sons-and-slaves rule is limited to פסח by the word 'בו', so it does not apply to תרומה.

steps.title: Then let 'בו' allow an uncircumcised man to eat תרומה
steps.stepSummary: If 'בו' limits rules to פסח, then 'no uncircumcised man shall eat from it' should mean he may eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, say this: 'No uncircumcised man shall eat from it.' From it, the פסח, he may not eat, but he may eat תרומה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer around. If 'בו' always limits things to פסח, the same word in the פסוק about an uncircumcised man should mean he is allowed to eat תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on an ערל eating פסח also says 'בו'. Using the same logic as step 14, that ban should apply only to פסח. That would let an uncircumcised כהן eat תרומה, which goes against the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: if so (if your logic is right)

phrases.english: If so, say:
"No uncircumcised man shall eat from it":
phrases.notes: שמות 12:48

phrases.english: from it he may not eat,
but he may eat תרומה!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אֵימָא: כׇּל עָרֵל לֹא יֹאכַל בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the method of step 14 against itself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word 'בו' appears in the ban on an ערל, so by the same reading an uncircumcised man should be allowed to eat תרומה.

steps.title: The גזירה שוה of 'תושב ושכיר' forbids him
steps.stepSummary: The words 'תושב ושכיר' appear by both פסח and תרומה, and that link teaches that an uncircumcised man may not eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written 'a sojourner and a hired servant'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the גזירה שוה from 'תושב ושכיר' already teaches that an ערל may not eat תרומה. So 'בו' cannot be used to allow him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here there is a clear source on the other side: the גזירה שוה brings the ban on an ערל over to תרומה. So in this case 'בו' does not win. That leaves one source for each case, and the next question is how we knew which goes where.

keyTerms.meaning: a sojourner and a hired worker (the shared words of the גזירה שוה)

phrases.english: But it is written "a sojourner and a hired servant"!
phrases.notes: These same words appear by פסח (שמות 12:45) and by תרומה (ויקרא 22:10). That shared wording is the גזירה שוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15 by pointing back to the גזירה שוה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A stronger source (the גזירה שוה) overrides the limiting word for an uncircumcised man.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'בו' should allow an uncircumcised man to eat תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גזירה שוה forbids an uncircumcised man from eating תרומה.

steps.title: Why give each source to that case?
steps.stepSummary: Why did we apply the גזירה שוה to a man's own ערלות and the limit of 'בו' to his sons and slaves, and not the reverse?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we made this choice. This is a setup line, and the next steps give the reasons on each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now have two sources pulling in opposite directions: the גזירה שוה includes a case in the ban on תרומה, and 'בו' leaves a case out. The question is why the man's own ערלות got the גזירה שוה and his sons and slaves got 'בו', and not the other way around.

keyTerms.meaning: and what did you see? (why did you choose this way?)

phrases.english: And what did you see?
phrases.notes: He's asking: why put his own ערלות into the ban and leave out his sons and slaves, and not the other way around?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that each case has its own source, the גמרא asks why the sources were split this way. It is the same kind of question as step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the גזירה שוה was given to the man's own ערלות and the limit 'בו' to his sons and slaves.

steps.title: A man's own ערלות is more serious
steps.stepSummary: It makes sense to include a man's own ערלות, because it involves his own body and carries the punishment of כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that his own ערלות is the one to include, since it is something about his own body, and it is punished with כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a man's own ערלות is the more serious case. So it is the more fitting case to include in the ban on eating תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two reasons are given. The missing מילה is on his own body, and not doing it carries כרת. A more serious case is the better one to include in a prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: it makes sense, it stands to reason
the punishment of being 'cut off', given by Heaven

phrases.english: It makes sense that his own ערלות
is the one to include,
since it is an act on his own body,
and it is punished with כרת.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִסְתַּבְּרָא עֲרֵלוּת דְּגוּפֵיהּ הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְרַבּוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A man's own ערלות is more serious (it is on his body and carries כרת), so it is the case to include.

steps.title: On the contrary: sons and slaves apply all the time
steps.stepSummary: The other side argues that the circumcision of sons and slaves should be the case included, because that duty can come up at any time.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! The circumcision of his males and slaves should be the one to include, since it applies at all times!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back with a reason for the other side. The duty to circumcise sons and slaves can come up at any time, so maybe that is the case to include.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man's own מילה is a one-time matter, but whenever a new son is born or a new slave is bought, a new duty to circumcise starts. That is a reason to treat it as stronger. This reopens the question of step 17, and Step 20 answers it.

phrases.english: On the contrary: the circumcision of his males and slaves
should be the one to include,
since it applies at all times!
phrases.notes: Any time he has a son or a slave who is not circumcised, he has a duty to circumcise him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה: מִילַת זְכָרָיו וַעֲבָדָיו הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְרַבּוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasons of step 18 with a reason for the other side, like step 10 did earlier.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 18 that a man's own ערלות is the more fitting case to include.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sons and slaves bring a duty that can apply at any time, which could make that case the stronger one to include.

steps.title: The reasons for a man's own ערלות are more numerous
steps.stepSummary: The reasons for applying the גזירה שוה to a man's own ערלות outweigh the one reason for applying it to his sons and slaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are more numerous.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 19. The side that says the גזירה שוה covers a man's own ערלות has more reasons behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 gave reasons for a man's own ערלות: it is in his own body, and it carries כרת. Step 19 gave only one reason for sons and slaves: that duty can come up at any time. When there are more reasons on one side, that side wins, so the גזירה שוה goes to the man's own ערלות.

phrases.english: These are more numerous.
phrases.notes: 'These' means the reasons from Step 18 for including his own ערלות: his own body, and כרת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 19 by weighing the reasons on each side.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Weighing of reasons: the side with more reasons wins
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The duty to circumcise sons and slaves, which can come up at any time, might be the case the גזירה שוה includes.
steps.terutzMaskana: A man's own ערלות has more reasons behind it, so the גזירה שוה applies to his own ערלות.

steps.title: Other people's ערלות cannot be stricter than his own
steps.stepSummary: Even without counting reasons, it is not logical for his sons' and slaves' ערלות to stop him from eating תרומה while his own ערלות does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: even without the point that these reasons are more numerous, you still could not say it. Is there anything where his own ערלות does not hold him back, but other people's ערלות does hold him back?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, stronger answer. It would be backwards for other people's ערלות to stop him from eating while his own ערלות does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose we said the reverse: the גזירה שוה covers sons and slaves, and 'בו' leaves his own ערלות out of the תרומה rule. Then an uncircumcised man could eat תרומה, but a circumcised man with an uncircumcised son could not. That is impossible, since his own ערלות must be at least as serious as anyone else's. So the only logical reading is the one the גמרא already gave.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces a second answer)
His own ערלות, in his own body
The ערלות of others (his sons and slaves)

steps.whatToRemember: The גזירה שוה from 'תושב ושכיר' teaches that a man's own ערלות stops him from eating תרומה. The limit of 'בו' means his sons' and slaves' ערלות stops him only from eating the פסח.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
Even without the point that these are more numerous,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: you could not say it.
phrases.notes: He means you could not say the גזירה שוה is about sons and slaves.

phrases.english: Is there anything
where his own ערלות does not hold him back,
but other people's ערלות does hold him back?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: בְּלָא הָנָךְ נְפִישָׁן נָמֵי לָא מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to Step 19 that does not depend on counting reasons.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical impossibility of the reverse reading (a lesser case cannot be stricter than a greater one)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the גזירה שוה includes sons and slaves, and 'בו' leaves out his own ערלות.
steps.terutzMaskana: That reverse reading would make others' ערלות stricter than his own, which cannot be, so the גזירה שוה must apply to his own ערלות.

steps.title: What does 'בו' teach about a בן נכר?
steps.stepSummary: If 'בו' is used for a דרשה, then the גמרא asks why 'בו' is needed in the פסוק 'כל בן נכר לא יאכל בו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have said 'from it' comes for a דרשה, why do I need 'from it' in 'No stranger shall eat from it'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. Since the word 'בו' was used to limit a rule to the פסח, what does the same word teach in the פסוק about a בן נכר?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא used 'בו' in 'ומלתה אותו אז יאכל בו' to teach that uncircumcised sons and slaves hold a man back only from the פסח, not from תרומה. The parallel reading of 'בו' by the ערל was rejected in Step 16, because of the גזירה שוה. Now the גמרא asks what 'בו' adds in the פסוק about the בן נכר. This sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: For a דרשה, to teach something extra
A stranger, someone cut off from ה׳'s service

phrases.english: Now that you have said:
'from it' comes for a דרשה,

phrases.aramaic: ״כׇּל בֶּן נֵכָר לֹא יֹאכַל בּוֹ״ — לְמָה לִי?
phrases.english: 'No stranger shall eat from it': why do I need it?
phrases.notes: שמות 12:43

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמְרַתְּ: בּוֹ לִדְרָשָׁה הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion that 'בו' is used for a דרשה and applies the same question to the בן נכר פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word 'בו' teaches in the פסוק 'כל בן נכר לא יאכל בו'.

steps.title: 'בו' limits the בן נכר rule to the פסח
steps.stepSummary: The answer begins: 'from it', meaning only the פסח. The full answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'From it'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer by repeating the word 'בו'. This tells us the בן נכר rule is limited to eating the פסח, and the answer is completed on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as 'בו' in 'ומלתה אותו אז יאכל בו' limited the sons-and-slaves rule to the פסח, 'בו' by the בן נכר does the same. The גמרא will now explain what is left out by that limit.

keyTerms.meaning: From it, meaning only from the פסח

phrases.english: From it
phrases.notes: The answer keeps going on the next amud: only from the פסח is he held back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question of Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'בו' teaches that the בן נכר is held back only from eating the פסח. The full details continue on the next amud.
